newsitem.title: UK: Harvey Nichols rises, seen as good value.
newsitem.headline: Harvey Nichols rises, seen as good value.

text.p: Shares in British luxury department store Harvey Nichols rose slightly on Friday, bucking a sharp market selloff, extended its gain from Thursday as the market saw good value in the stock.
"It had been discounted quite heavily, trading was quite weak last season," said one analyst. "But now it is looking quite cheap."
At 1338 GMT, the stock was up 6p at 260-1/2p, a one-month high, after gaining 12-1/2 on Thursday.
"Sales have been pretty good over the last six weeks, it has been one of the winners in the market place," said Robert Clark, director of retail analysts Corporate Intelligence Group.
On August 6 the company said cumulative sales for the first 18 weeks of the current financial year were up 19 percent on the same period last year.
Buying by the influx of summer tourists and income from their Leeds store in the North of England, which opened in mid-October, had helped boost sales, Clark said.
